about: Agents beyond the twelve this plugin reads directly. An agent is listed only if it is still maintained AND has a working way to read usage or plan limits (an Omarchy usage record, or a documented CLI command or API): see each entry's `maintained` and `reads`. usageType says how it reports usage; `unsure` flags a claim that could not be fully verified. Researched 2026-11-22.

session_weekly.label: Session and weekly limits
session_weekly.tabNote: Has rolling session and weekly limits.

monthly_credits.label: Monthly credits
monthly_credits.tabNote: Usage comes out of a monthly credit allowance.

request_count.label: Request count
request_count.tabNote: Limited by a number of requests per day.

byok_no_limits.label: Bring your own key
byok_no_limits.tabNote: Bring your own key: it adds no limit of its own, so nothing to show here. Any cap is your provider's.

no_usage_data.label: No usage data
no_usage_data.tabNote: Has usage limits but publishes no way to read them, so none are shown.

agents.name: Qwen Code
agents.note: The free Qwen OAuth tier was cut to 100 requests/day on 2026-04-13 and discontinued on 2026-04-15. Now it runs on an API key or an Alibaba Coding Plan; Omarchy notes no way to read that plan's quota.
agents.unsure: No official Alibaba pricing page was reachable. Older posts still cite 2,000 requests/day, which is out of date. Coding Plan limits are unverified.
agents.reads: Omarchy's qwen usage record: tokens by model and day from Qwen Code's local session transcripts. No plan limit can be read.
agents.maintained: Qwen Code 0.17.x is on npm and its changelog has entries through April 2026.

agents.name: Mistral Vibe
agents.note: Included with Le Chat Pro ($14.99/mo) and Team, with pay-as-you-go beyond the plan budget, or your own API key. Mistral publishes no numeric usage limits (Omarchy's own notes say the same).
agents.reads: Omarchy's vibe usage record: tokens from Mistral Vibe's local session logs. Mistral publishes no numeric plan limit.
agents.maintained: Mistral announced Vibe 2.0 and sells it with Le Chat Pro and Team.

agents.name: DeepSeek Harness
agents.note: DeepSeek's open agent harness (developer preview). You pay DeepSeek per token from a prepaid balance (HTTP 402 at zero); the harness adds no limit of its own. This plugin never shows purchasable balances.
agents.unsure: Developer preview, and the name dsh is also used by community CLIs. The granted-credit expiry window is not published.
agents.reads: Omarchy's deepseek usage record: tokens from dsh session logs, plus DeepSeek's balance endpoint (purchasable balances are never shown by this plugin).
agents.maintained: DeepSeek's open harness is in developer preview with Ollama and DeepSeek integration docs.

agents.name: MiniMax Code
agents.note: Plans have a 5-hour window and a 7-day window (video models only the weekly one), both starting at first use and resetting independently. /status in mcode or `mmx quota` shows usage; exact counts per tier aren't published.
agents.reads: Omarchy's minimax usage record: the 5-hour and weekly windows (also `/status` in mcode and `mmx quota`).
agents.maintained: MiniMax's M Plan docs describe MiniMax Code with current usage rules (2026).

agents.name: OpenClaw
agents.note: A gateway agent that reuses your provider keys or subscriptions (Codex, Claude CLI, Coding Plans); it has no limits of its own. `openclaw status --usage` shows your providers' quota windows.
agents.unsure: The field names inside a usage window are not documented and no populated sample was available (the provider here reported an error), so the reader accepts several spellings and shows a bar only when a percent is really present. Reusing a Claude subscription is described as unsettled; check Anthropic's terms.
agents.reads: `openclaw status --usage --json` (documented): usage.providers[].windows[] for the providers it is signed in to. Read by bin/openclaw-usage.mjs.
agents.maintained: OpenClaw's docs are versioned monthly (2026.7.1 seen).
agents.tabText:
Bring your own key, no limits of its own.
Usage depends on your model provider.

dropped.aider: archived/inactive; also nothing of its own to read
dropped.cline: no CLI command or API reads ClinePass usage (dashboard only)
dropped.goose: bring your own key: no plan limits or usage of its own to read
dropped.crush: bring your own key: nothing to read (Charm Hyper limits unpublished)
dropped.kilo: only an undocumented balance endpoint; prepaid balances aren't shown
dropped.openhands: its credits API is a purchasable balance (cloud only)
dropped.plandex: cloud shut down; nothing to read
dropped.pi: bring your own key: nothing of its own to read
dropped.omp: bring your own key: nothing of its own to read
dropped.commandcode: only a third-party tool reads its usage; no official command or API
dropped.droid: Factory's analytics endpoint (/cost/me/query) needs an Enterprise org (403 enterprise_required otherwise) and returns credits consumed only, never remaining allowance or window limits; /limits works only inside Droid.
dropped.auggie: Augment documents no command or API that returns remaining credits (only per-run --show-cost and an Enterprise dashboard); auggie account status and its web endpoints are third-party, unverified.
